discovery: Discovery of the two-dimensional electron gas and emergent quantum phenomena at complex oxide interfaces

nominees.name: Harold Y. Hwang
nominees.affiliation: Stanford University and SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory, USA

nominees.name: Akira Ohtomo
nominees.affiliation: Institute of Science Tokyo (formerly Tokyo Institute of Technology), Japan

nominees.name: Jochen Mannhart
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute for Solid State Research, Stuttgart, Germany

subfield: Condensed matter physics: correlated oxide heterostructures and interfaces
motivation: In 2004 Ohtomo and Hwang showed that atomically sharp interfaces between two band insulators, LaAlO3 and SrTiO3, host a high-mobility two-dimensional electron gas. This showed that the interface itself can be a new electronic material. Mannhart and co-workers established a critical thickness for conduction, electric-field switching of the conducting state, and interface superconductivity. Coexisting magnetism and gate-tunable superconductivity followed. Together these results created the field of oxide interface physics. Polar discontinuity, orbital reconstruction and spin-orbit coupling can now be engineered layer by layer to produce states that do not exist in the bulk constituents. The approach has shaped research worldwide, from nickelate superconductivity in thin films, discovered in Hwang's group, to oxide electronics and nanoscale devices. It is a paradigm shift in how physicists design quantum matter, and it grew from collaboration between Japan, the United States and Europe.
